notes: Nine hand-picked sentences across English, Italian, Spanish, French, German, Japanese and Chinese. This is a small regression comparison, not general translation accuracy.
Keyword hits do not establish semantic correctness. Clean outputs exclude reasoning tags and prompt labels. Per-request timings exclude model loading; prompt lengths and output lengths differ.
LFM does not list Italian or Chinese among its supported languages. This mixed-language fixture is not a supported-languages-only ranking.

All prompt formats were tested for all four models. LFM Instruct did best with plain ChatML, LFM Base with parallel text, Qwen Instruct with ChatML and a forced empty thinking block, Qwen Base with parallel text or ChatML.
The old empty-thinking prompt caused both LFM versions to copy unrelated greetings (0/9). LFM Base still echoed several English sources with parallel text.

Qwen Base parallel text mistranslated the English train sentence into Italian. Its Chinese-to-English output omitted arrival and inserted an unsupported grammatical construction. Its Japanese output omitted the explicit help phrase. These issues can pass keyword checks.
Both Qwen variants mistranslated train as station in Italian under the original prompt. Qwen Base also added home in one Chinese-to-English result with plain ChatML.
Only base Q4_K_M models are in the app catalog. Instruct files are retained solely for the comparison. Translation uses the same Qwen Base weights as prediction.

The follow-up prompt probe added four greeting/question cases and tested all four prompt formats on Qwen Base (52 evaluations). Every format had failures; explicit language labels did not fix Buonasera becoming Good morning in the raw formats.

Base Qwen passed the five-case translation service and cancellation check. The translation UI regression failed because Buonasera was translated as Good morning instead of Good evening. This remains a model quality limitation of the selected base-only configuration, not a passing integration result.
